items.title: Right of residence for EU/EEA students (no permit)
items.title_it: Diritto di soggiorno per studenti UE/SEE (nessun permesso)
items.summary: EU/EEA citizens need no residence permit to study in Sweden. Up to 3 months a valid passport or ID card is enough; beyond 3 months you must meet the right-of-residence conditions (e.g. studying or having sufficient funds). You cannot register your right of residence with Migrationsverket and do not need to contact it.

interpretations.hypothesis: Stockholm University: registered students with comprehensive health insurance automatically have right of residence, i.e. comprehensive insurance is a condition for students.
Migrationsverket's EU/EEA page lists only 'studying or having sufficient funds' and does not mention health insurance.

items.notes: Whether an EHIC counts as 'comprehensive health insurance' for the right of residence was not confirmed on an official page.

items.title: Residence permit for Swiss students (free, start studying on arrival)
items.title_it: Permesso di soggiorno per studenti svizzeri (gratuito, si può iniziare all'arrivo)
items.summary: Swiss citizens staying more than 3 months need a residence permit. Requirements: admission to a course at least at upper-secondary level, comprehensive private health insurance for the whole stay and a written assurance of funds. Applying is free; the permit covers the studies, max 1 year at a time (renewable), and you may study and work while waiting for the decision.

items.title: Residence permit for studies (non-EU students)
items.title_it: Permesso di soggiorno per studio (studenti extra-UE)

other: full-time studies (30 credits/semester); distance learning does not qualify
tuition fee paid before applying, if fee-paying

items.summary: Non-EU students admitted to full-time studies longer than 3 months need a residence permit (also exchange students, per Stockholm University). You must show maintenance of SEK 10,656/month (applications in 2026; SEK 10,584 in 2025) for the whole permit period, paid tuition, and comprehensive health insurance if studies last under one year. Permits are granted for 1–2 years, never longer than the studies.
steps: Get final admission and pay any tuition fee
Apply via Migrationsverket's e-service (or on paper at an embassy)
Show passport digitally or in person; attend interview if asked
items.cost: SEK 1,500 application fee for adults, SEK 750 under 18 (2026); not refunded if rejected
items.notes: Maintenance amount is reduced if food or housing is provided free (SEK 2,960 and SEK 4,736/month, 2026). 75% of recent cases decided within three months.

items.title: Population register (folkbokföring) for stays of 1 year or more
items.title_it: Iscrizione all'anagrafe (folkbokföring) per soggiorni di almeno 1 anno

applies_to.stay_duration: plan to live in Sweden for at least one year
other: EU/EEA citizens must prove right of residence
non-EU citizens need a Swedish residence permit

items.summary: You should be registered if you plan to live in Sweden for one year or more; then you receive a personnummer. Students must show enrolment and admission notice, means of support and ID; Skatteverket decides. Notify via the 'Moving to Sweden' e-service (at the earliest 14 days before moving) and book an in-person identity check at a service centre as soon as possible after arrival.
steps: Submit the 'Moving to Sweden' notification (earliest 14 days before moving)
Book and attend an identity check in person at a state service centre
Wait for the decision (about 5 weeks before a case is assigned to an administrator)
items.deadline: No fixed day-count stated on the page; identity check 'as soon as possible' after arrival

interpretations.hypothesis: Students with studies under 12 months are generally not registered (they may need a coordination number instead).
For studies under 12 months Skatteverket asks for more information on what you will do after your studies, so registration may still be possible case by case.

items.title: Personal identity number (personnummer)

applies_to.stay_duration: registered in the Population Register (stay of at least one year)

items.summary: Skatteverket assigns a personnummer when you are first listed in the Population Register. It is needed for most everyday services (e.g. BankID, Swish, full bank services).

items.title: Coordination number (samordningsnummer) for stays under 1 year
items.title_it: Numero di coordinamento (samordningsnummer) per soggiorni sotto 1 anno

other: never registered in the Population Register
must show a connection to Sweden and a need for the number

items.summary: A coordination number is an identifier for people not in the Population Register. You can apply yourself if staying under one year, or a public authority, university or college can request one for you. An in-person identity check at a service centre is required; the number stays active for five years.
items.notes: Processing: up to 6 weeks before an individual application is assigned to an administrator. Needed e.g. to register for A-tax or apply for SINK when working.

items.title: Tax on work income: SINK 22.5% for limited tax liability
items.title_it: Tasse sul lavoro: SINK al 22,5% per chi non è fiscalmente residente

other: applies if you do not live in Sweden, do not stay at least six consecutive months and have no significant connection to Sweden

items.summary: People with limited tax liability can pay SINK, a final tax of 22.5% with no deductions or tax return; they may instead choose ordinary A-tax. Living and working in Sweden for a year or more usually means ordinary Swedish income tax. Register for A-tax or apply for SINK quoting your coordination number.
items.notes: The page has no student-specific rules.

items.title: Healthcare with the EHIC (EU/EEA/Swiss students)
items.title_it: Cure mediche con la TEAM (studenti UE/SEE/svizzeri)
items.summary: Order an EHIC in your home country before coming; with it you pay the same as people insured in Sweden for care that cannot wait. If you are registered in the Population Register you are generally entitled to care at the Swedish patient fee. Försäkringskassan assesses case by case whether you are insured in Sweden; working in Sweden during studies can make you insured here.
items.authority: Försäkringskassan (Swedish Social Insurance Agency); regional healthcare (1177)
items.cost: patient fees as for residents with EHIC
items.notes: You cannot be covered by two countries' social insurance at the same time. A physical ID is required at care units (digital IDs not accepted, per 1177).

items.title: Health insurance for non-EU students
items.summary: For studies under one year the residence permit requires comprehensive health insurance valid for the whole stay (emergency and other care, hospitalisation, emergency dental, medical repatriation). For studies of at least one year you should register in the Population Register, which gives access to healthcare. Without coverage, non-EU patients usually pay the full cost of care.
items.notes: Exceptions to full-cost care exist for some countries (e.g. Algeria, Australia, Chile, Israel, Turkey, Quebec). Many universities provide Kammarkollegiet insurance (see subsidies.json).

items.title: Opening a bank account
items.summary: Available services depend heavily on having a personnummer. Without one, banks generally give no card for online payments (only in-store and cash); SEB has been more willing to accept international students. Swish and BankID require a personnummer. Bring acceptance letter, passport, address proof, and a residence permit if non-EU/Swiss.
items.notes: Source is a university guidance page, not a bank or regulator.

items.title: Student ID needed for student fares
items.title_it: Tessera studente necessaria per le tariffe studenti

other: rules and minimum study load differ by regional operator

items.summary: Student fares require a digital student ID showing the student travel symbol (apps from Mecenat, Studentkortet/STUK, Hitract, WeStudents or Orbi) plus a valid ID document. Västtrafik: CSN-eligible studies, at least part time for 10 consecutive weeks; UL: at least 75% studies; SL: full-time students meeting SL's conditions.
items.authority: Regional transport operators (SL, Västtrafik, Skånetrafiken, UL)
items.notes: Discount amounts and prices are in subsidies.json (category transport) and the city files.

items.title: Working as an EU/EEA or non-fee-paying student
items.title_it: Lavorare da studente UE/SEE o non pagante
items.summary: Students who are not fee-paying (EU/EEA and Swiss citizens) have no limit on working hours. Swiss students may work while their permit application is pending.

items.title: Work limit for non-EU students: 15 hours/week
items.title_it: Limite di lavoro per studenti extra-UE: 15 ore a settimana

other: bachelor's or master's level residence permit for studies granted on or after 11 June 2026

items.summary: Bachelor's and master's students may work max 15 hours/week if the study permit was granted on or after 11 June 2026; exceeding it can lead to withdrawal or refused extension. Exceptions: work in June–August, internships within the programme, student representation/research at the institution, and after completing at least two semesters (if not applying for a new sub-doctoral study permit).

interpretations.hypothesis: The 15 h/week limit applies to permits granted on or after 11 June 2026.
University of Gothenburg states the new rules took effect on 1 June 2026, limiting students with study permits to 15 h/week during semesters.

items.notes: The Migrationsverket page does not state the rule for permits granted before 11 June 2026, nor how the weekly hours are counted.

items.title: No statutory minimum wage (collective agreements)
items.summary: Sweden has no national minimum wage (Eurostat, as of 1 July 2026); wage floors are set in sector collective agreements. Example: hotel and restaurant agreement (Gröna Riksavtalet) from 1 April 2026, no prior experience: SEK 153.64–164.30/hour; separate youth rates apply under 20.
items.authority: Eurostat; HRF (Hotel and Restaurant Workers' Union)
items.notes: Collective-agreement floors apply only to employers bound by the agreement; the HRF figures are one sector, not a national floor.
